text:
Winnipeg's season has been one long answer to a single question: who stops the puck now that Connor Hellebuyck is in New Jersey? For most of the fall it has been Stuart Skinner, with 16 of 25 starts and 34 saves in Monday's win over Utah. Tonight, on the first stop of a road trip, the Jets hand the night to Nico Daws instead. He has played nine games at a .891 save rate and sits almost exactly at zero saves above expected (-0.3), which is the definition of a goalie who has neither won nor lost games on his own. In Boston, against a team that takes 53% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets), that is a real test.

The Jets are 3-1-1 in their last five and riding some history. Mark Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk as the franchise's all-time goal scorer last weekend, Gabriel Vilardi scored three against Utah, and Kyle Connor is our likeliest scorer on the ice at 44%. Our numbers flag Connor and Scheifele as running hot, and Dawson Mercer's five goals in ten games come on ordinary chances. Dylan DeMelo is out four to six weeks, which leaves the right side thin in front of a backup.

Boston has been better than its recent record. The Bruins lost three straight earlier this month while winning the chance battle each night, then beat Detroit and Washington, the second one on Elias Lindholm's four-goal night. His 11 points in ten games are earned: the chances have gone up with the goals. The season is running hot overall, though, with 7.8 goals of extra finishing and 10.2 from goaltending, and Jeremy Swayman (+6.5) is a big part of that.

James Hagens stays out, and Marat Khusnutdinov has his spot beside Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt. He is our depth sleeper at 17% to score, because his shots have come from dangerous places and the Jets allow the sixth-most expected goals per 60. Watch the penalty box too: Boston takes 4.8 penalties a game. The playoff race leans Boston's way, 83% to Winnipeg's 32%.
headline: Nico Daws gets the Boston crease
